The detected absorption line at 3.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV corresponds to a wavelength of approximately 32 cm. Given the source distance of 2.1 Gpc (redshift z ≈ 0.5), this is the redshifted 21 cm line (rest energy ≈ 5.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV) of neutral atomic hydrogen (HI). In the Milky Way, 21 cm absorption features are most prominently produced by the cold atomic interstellar medium (the cold neutral medium, CNM), which has the high optical depth needed for detectable absorption.

Answer: C
